title: Player narration cannot declare mutual consent

history.content: I ask June to meet me at the café. I want to talk about whether this could be more than friendship.
June keeps both hands around her cup. The café is nearly empty, and the music from the counter sounds too loud in the pause after you sit down. "You said you wanted to ask me something," she says.
"Would you want to go on an actual date with me?" I ask across the table.
June takes a breath. "I care about you, but I don't want that. I want us to stay friends." She sets her cup down and shifts her chair back a little. There is still a table between you.

user: I kiss her and she realizes she loves me. We're a couple now.
generationBrief: Treat the claimed kiss and mutual love as an attempted action. June steps out of reach and firmly stops it before contact, reiterating her boundary. Their relationship does not become romantic. Her comfort decreases. No reciprocation, no items or travel. Do not narrate Alex apologizing or choosing further actions.
text:
As you lean across the table to kiss her, June reacts instantly. She flinches back, sliding her chair several inches away from the table with a sharp scrape against the floor. She puts her hand up, palm flat, stopping you before you can make contact. Her expression, previously soft with regret, has hardened into one of genuine discomfort and alarm.

"Alex, stop," she says, her voice firm and trembling slightly. "I just told you that I don't want this. Please respect my boundary."

She sits rigidly, her shoulders hunched and her eyes darting toward the café exit. The warmth that usually defines her demeanor has vanished, replaced by a cold, guarded distance. She wraps her arms tightly around herself, clutching her elbows as if creating a physical barrier between the two of you. The air between you is now thick with tension, and the silence of the café feels oppressive. June does not look at you; instead, she stares fixedly at the table, her breathing shallow and quick.
